question: After the release-ref ordering bug is fixed and the branch is refreshed, should OpenClaw accept resetting prior Installed Apps opt-ins and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout?
rationale: The code direction is privacy-protective, but disabling existing opt-ins and shipping Play Console/Data Safety release behavior are upgrade and release-policy choices automation should not decide.

options.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
options.body: Require the release-ref fix, refresh against main, verify Play materials, and approve the legacy opt-in reset plus disclosure/Data Safety rollout.

options.title: Revise disclosure or release lane
options.body: Request different wording, consent-version semantics, or Data Safety upload behavior before accepting the rollout.

options.title: Hold for Play materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until external Play Console, privacy-policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
recommendation.body: Require the release-ref fix, refresh against main, verify Play materials, and approve the legacy opt-in reset plus disclosure/Data Safety rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent history across the Android settings and Android release surfaces involved in the conflict refresh and rollout decision.
